bib.title: Aggregated Residual Transformations for Deep Neural Networks

question: Can a homogeneous multi-branch residual block with a new dimension, cardinality, improve image classification accuracy beyond depth and width at fixed complexity?
hypothesis: Increasing cardinality is a more effective way of gaining accuracy than going deeper or wider.
contributions: ResNeXt: a block that aggregates C same-topology transformations by summation, with few hyper-parameters
Cardinality as a measurable dimension besides depth and width
Gains over ResNet on ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-5K, CIFAR, COCO; 2nd place ILSVRC 2016 classification

method.summary: Replace ResNet bottleneck blocks with blocks of C parallel low-dimensional bottleneck paths summed (implemented as grouped convolution). Compare cardinality vs width vs depth at matched or doubled FLOPs on ImageNet-1K, then ImageNet-5K, CIFAR and COCO.

datasets.name: ImageNet-1K
datasets.split: train / val, evaluated on val with single 224x224 center crop of image with shorter side 256
datasets.preprocessing: 224x224 random crop from resized image, scale and aspect ratio augmentation of [38] via fb.resnet.torch

datasets.name: ImageNet-5K
datasets.split: no official split; evaluated on original ImageNet-1K val
datasets.source: Subset of ImageNet-22K: the 1K classes plus the 4000 other classes with most images

datasets.name: CIFAR-10 / CIFAR-100
datasets.preprocessing: 32x32 random crop from zero-padded 40x40 or flip

datasets.name: COCO
datasets.size: 80k train + 35k val subset for training; 5k minival for eval

models.name: ResNeXt-50 (32x4d)
models.architecture: ResNet with grouped-conv bottleneck blocks, C=32, d=4

models.name: ResNeXt-29 (8x64d, 16x64d)
models.architecture: bottleneck template, 3 stages x 3 blocks, CIFAR

training.objective: softmax classification (inferred: cross-entropy; Faster R-CNN losses for detection)
training.lr: 0.1 (ImageNet and CIFAR); detection RPN 0.02 then 0.002, Fast R-CNN 0.005 then 0.0005
training.lr_schedule: ImageNet: divide by 10 three times, schedule of [11]; CIFAR: reduced at epochs 150 and 225
training.batch_size: 256 on 8 GPUs (32 per GPU) ImageNet; 128 on 8 GPUs CIFAR
training.epochs: ImageNet-1K: 90 (read from Fig 5 axis); CIFAR: 300; ImageNet-5K: same number of mini-batches as 1K, so 1/5 epochs
training.regularisation: batch norm after convs; data augmentation
training.seeds: CIFAR: average of 10 runs; ImageNet: not stated

other.shortcuts: identity, projection (type B) when dims increase
other.downsampling: stride-2 in 3x3 layer of first block in conv3-5
other.detection: Faster R-CNN, RPN and Fast R-CNN not feature-shared; RPN 2 images/GPU, 256 anchors; Fast R-CNN 1 image/GPU, 64 regions; pretrained on ImageNet-1K

inference.samples: single 224x224 center crop in ablations; also 320x320 single crop; multi-scale dense testing for competition

eval.protocol: Single runs on ImageNet (no variance reported); 10 runs on CIFAR with standard error bars in Fig 7.

results.claim: ResNeXt-50 32x4d beats ResNet-50 at matched complexity on ImageNet-1K
results.setup: ImageNet-1K val, single 224 crop, ~4.1B FLOPs, ~25M params, 90 epochs
results.quote: the 32×4d ResNeXt-50 has a validation error of 22.2%, which is 1.7% lower than the ResNet baseline’s 23.9%

results.claim: Doubling cardinality (64x4d ResNeXt-101) beats going deeper or wider at 2x ResNet-101 FLOPs
results.setup: ImageNet-1K val, single 224 crop, ~15B FLOPs; ResNet-200 21.7, wider ResNet-101 21.3
results.table: Table 4, row ResNeXt-101 64 × 4d, column top-1 err

results.claim: ResNeXt-101 32x4d beats ResNet-101 at same complexity
results.table: Table 3, row ResNeXt-101 32 × 4d, column top-1 error (%)

results.quote: achieving a single-crop top-5 error rate of 4.4%

results.claim: ImageNet-5K: ResNeXt-50 lowers 5K-way top-1 error vs ResNet-50
results.setup: Trained on ImageNet-5K (6.8M images), tested on 1K val as 5K-way; ResNet-50 45.5
CIFAR-10, 68.1M params, mean of 10 runs; Wide ResNet 4.17
results.quote: Our larger method achieves 3.58% test error (average of 10 runs) on CIFAR-10 and 17.31% on CIFAR-100

results.setup: CIFAR-100, 68.1M params, mean of 10 runs; Wide ResNet 20.50

results.claim: COCO minival AP with ResNeXt-50 backbone in Faster R-CNN
results.setup: COCO minival, Faster R-CNN, ImageNet-1K pretrained; ResNet-50 26.5; AP@0.5 49.7 vs 47.6

results.claim: Removing shortcuts hurts ResNet-50 far more than ResNeXt-50
results.setup: ImageNet-1K, ResNeXt-50 32x4d without residual; ResNet-50 without residual 31.2
results.quote: Removing shortcuts from the ResNeXt-50 increases the error by 3.9 points to 26.1%

results.claim: Training overhead of grouped-conv ResNeXt-101 32x4d vs ResNet-101
results.setup: 8x NVIDIA M40, Torch built-in grouped conv; ResNet-101 0.70s
results.quote: takes 0.95s per mini-batch, vs. 0.70s of ResNet-101

results.claim: 64x4d ResNeXt-101 training takes 10 days on 8 GPUs
results.quote: takes 1.7s per mini-batch and 10 days total on 8 GPUs

limits: ImageNet gains are single-run with no variance reported
Gains shrink at ResNet-101 depth (0.8 points) and on COCO 101-layer
Grouped conv implementation is brute-force; 0.95s vs 0.70s per mini-batch
Saturating accuracy as width drops below 4d; authors do not go below 4d
Generalisation to non-visual tasks is only expected, not tested
